newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up 1/8 in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up 1/8 in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices were up 1/8 point midway through Monday's listless pre-holiday session, traders said.
"The (muni) market is kind of firm," one trader said, citing "a good bidside," but "very light activity."

A lack of supply and some recent bond friendly economic data was lending municipals a better tone, the trader said. He pointed to Friday's November durable goods report which showed a 1.6 percent drop in orders.
"People think the market is going to do better here...I think they are viewing a deceleration of the economy more than anything else," the trader said.

A second trader also judged muni cash 1/8 point higher in light trade ahead of Tuesday's New Year's Eve celebrations. PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended a 1400 EST close for Tuesday.
In the goverment market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off its highs but up 3/32 at 99-19/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 3/32 at 117-3/32. The March T-bond contract was up 2/32 at 114. The MOB spread was 99 ticks.

Unlike Friday's durables report, midmorning numbers Monday showed strength. The American Production and Inventory Control Society business outlook index rebounded to 51.8 in December from 46.8 in November.

Also Monday, the National Association of Realtors said U.S. November existing home sales rose 1.8 percent to a 4.04 million annual rate. Lending support to bonds, however, was a strong U.S. dollar, which held firm in overnight trade in Europe and Tokyo.
While no negotiated deals are expected this week, several large issues are slated for next week including a $346 million Houston, Texas, refunding deal via PaineWebber Inc.
